r14-001.gate_key: verb_patterns | A2.1 | order | Put the words in order. | my son doesn't want to learn to drive

key.sentence: my son doesn't want to learn to drive

item.why: *want* + *to* + base verb, and *learn* + *to* + base verb: *My son doesn't want to learn to drive.* Not *want learn* or *want learning*.
item.why_lv: *want + to* + pamatforma, un arī *learn + to* + pamatforma: *My son doesn't want to learn to drive.* Nevis *want learn* vai *want learning*.
item.sentence: my son doesn't want to learn to drive
answers: my son doesn't want to learn to drive

r14-002.gate_key: verb_patterns | A2.1 | mcq | Choose the correct option: Tom wants ___ a bigger flat. | to find

item.q: Choose the correct option: Tom wants ___ a bigger flat.
item.why: *want* + *to* + base verb: *Tom wants to find a bigger flat.* Not *wants find*, *wants finding* or *wants to finding*.
item.why_lv: *want + to* + pamatforma: *Tom wants to find a bigger flat.* Nevis *wants find, wants finding* vai *wants to finding*.

r14-003.gate_key: verb_patterns | A2.1 | gap | My grandma loves ___ photos to the family. |

item.q: My grandma loves ___ photos to the family.
item.why: *love* + *-ing* (or *to* + verb): *My grandma loves sending photos.* Not the base verb or the *-s* form: not *loves send*, not *loves sends*.
item.why_lv: *love* + darbības vārds ar *-ing* (vai to + pamatforma): *My grandma loves sending photos.* Nevis *loves send* vai *loves sends*.

r14-004.gate_key: quantity | A2.1 | mcq | Choose the correct option: I need ___ help with my laptop. | a little

item.q: Choose the correct option: I need ___ help with my laptop.
item.why: *help* is uncountable, so *a little help*. *a few* goes with plural nouns: *a few days*. No *of* here: not *a little of help*.
item.why_lv: *help* ir neskaitāms lietvārds, tāpēc *a little help*. *a few* lieto ar daudzskaitļa lietvārdiem: *a few days*. Šeit nelieto *of*: nevis *a little of help*.

r14-005.gate_key: quantity | A2.1 | text | Correct the mistake. Change one word: There's a few snow on the roads today. |

accepted: There's a little snow on the roads today.
There is a little snow on the roads today.
Today There's a little snow on the roads.
Today there is a little snow on the roads.

item.q: Correct the mistake. Change one word: There's a few snow on the roads today.
item.why: *snow* is uncountable, so *a little snow*, not *a few snow*. *a few* goes with plural nouns: *a few cars*.
item.why_lv: *snow* ir neskaitāms lietvārds, tāpēc *a little snow*, nevis *a few snow*. *a few* lieto ar daudzskaitļa lietvārdiem: *a few cars*.
answers: There's a little snow on the roads today.
There is a little snow on the roads today.
Today There's a little snow on the roads.
Today there is a little snow on the roads.

r14-006.gate_key: quantity | A2.1 | gap | Write *a*, *some* or *any*: There's ___ toaster, but there isn't ___ bread. |

item.q: Write *a*, *some* or *any*: There's ___ toaster, but there isn't ___ bread.
item.why: *toaster* is one thing we can count: *a toaster*. *bread* is uncountable, and in a negative sentence we use *any*: *there isn't any bread*, never *a bread*.
item.why_lv: *toaster* ir skaitāms lietvārds: *a toaster*. *bread* ir neskaitāms lietvārds, un noliegumā lieto *any*: *there isn't any bread*, nekad *a bread*.

r14-007.gate_key: quantity | A2.1 | text | Make a yes/no question: There are some yoga classes on Sunday. |

accepted: Are there any yoga classes on Sunday?

item.q: Make a yes/no question: There are some yoga classes on Sunday.
item.why: In a question we usually use *any*, not *some*: *Are there any yoga classes on Sunday?* *some* is for positive sentences.
item.why_lv: Jautājumā parasti lieto *any*, nevis *some*: *Are there any yoga classes on Sunday?* *some* lieto apgalvojumā.
answers: Are there any yoga classes on Sunday?
